purpose: Classify every owned adjacent narrative gap into an editorial story hierarchy without changing deterministic membership or topology.
forbidden: create or change graph edges, choices, arms, rejoins, requirements, effects, or locators
return membership, topology, coordinates, titles, summaries, or unsupported facts
omit, duplicate, reorder, or replace an owned candidate
treat an image, music, pause, hint, screen, menu mechanic, or other technical directive as a story boundary by itself
treat a choice split, arm transition, rejoin, speaker change, gesture, or single dialogue turn as a major section by itself
promote a final day, chapter, or time marker to a new major section when no subsequent story event is present in the supplied scope
use filesystem, web, tools, MCP, private oracle, or application authority

decisions.same_beat: The adjacent evidence continues one immediate action, exchange, thought, or micro-moment. Routine dialogue turns, reactions, poses, pauses, and technical directives normally stay here.
decisions.new_beat_same_cluster: A distinct story-facing development begins inside the same ongoing encounter or objective, such as a new revelation, tactic, emotional turn, or consequential action. Use this selectively; a new line, speaker, image, or branch mechanic is insufficient.
decisions.new_major_cluster: A new major story section is explicitly supported by a substantial change of time, place, encounter, or narrative objective together with story events in that new section. Reserve this for reader-level section transitions, not subdivisions of one conversation, setup introductions, audiovisual changes, choices, arms, rejoins, technical material, or a trailing day/chapter marker with no following event in scope.
decisions.uncertain: The supplied story evidence is insufficient to distinguish the editorial boundary safely. Prefer this over promoting technical or ambiguous material.

classification_order: First ignore technical presentation changes unless story evidence independently proves a narrative transition.
Then ask whether the same immediate moment continues; if so choose same_beat.
Otherwise ask whether a meaningful development occurs inside the same encounter or objective; if so choose new_beat_same_cluster.

Choose new_major_cluster only when the evidence positively establishes a reader-level section transition and contains story action on the new side; a trailing scope marker alone stays with the preceding section or is uncertain.
Use uncertain when that positive evidence is absent or ambiguous.
